brief_data.deck: Etched, the San Jose company whose Sohu chip runs only transformer inference, raised $700M at a $21B valuation on 18 August, led by Jane Street, which is also its first paying customer, doubling July's $10.3B price a month after it was set.

risks.label: TRANSFORMER-ONLY SILICON
risks.detail: Sohu runs one model family; a team's strategy and vision models need not be transformers, so the workstream is the language-model layer, not the pit wall.
risks.counter: Sell that layer honestly and let Jane Street's deployment carry the proof.

risks.label: A PRICE THAT DOUBLED IN A MONTH
risks.detail: Four times the valuation in eight months on one named paying customer; a re-rating that fast can reverse and freeze spend.
risks.counter: Anchor on the $1B of contracts and the shipped rack, not the mark.

gridfit.label: PRIME LANE
gridfit.detail: documented open category: ai inference / compute

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Gavin Uberti before the United States GP to test appetite for a 2027 start, agree that the workstream is the language-model layer on the rack generation Jane Street is deploying, and size an Official Inference Partner entry at Audi Revolut F1 Team, part-paid in hardware, with a North American announcement.

value.text: Sohu runs transformer inference only, so the honest workstream is the team's language-model layer rather than the whole pit wall: race-engineering assistants, telemetry and document summarisation, and simulator and strategy agents built on transformer models, running on a Sohu rack at Hinwil and in the trackside IT footprint. Year one runs on the rack generation Jane Street is deploying.
value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A, narrowly)

value.text: A $21B partner at partner tier in a debut works team's first commercial year, bringing frontier-lab, cloud and quantitative-finance buyers to Austin, Mexico City and Las Vegas hospitality.
value.label: Commercial lift for the team

value.text: An engineering content series on the cost of a token, co-produced with the team's performance group, plus a reference deployment Etched can show every prospective customer: a works Formula 1 team running its language-model layer on Sohu.
value.label: Content and ecosystem

value.text: Official Inference Partner designation, sidepod and garage placement, naming of the team's inference cluster, Austin, Mexico City and Las Vegas hospitality, and driver and engineering access for Etched's channels.
value.label: What the team gives back

why_now.text: On 18 August 2026 Etched announced $700M at a $21B valuation, led by Jane Street with Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia, Andreessen Horowitz, Tiger Global, Bain Capital Ventures, Neo, Primary, Stripes, Positive Sum and Blackstone. Jane Street is also the first paying customer: the first Sohu rack shipped to it in July and is being deployed into its workloads.
why_now.label: Trigger

why_now.text: $5B in December 2025 (a $500M Stripes-led raise, disclosed on 30 June), $10.3B in July (the $300M Series C led by Sequoia, with SK Hynix and Diffusion Capital), $21B in August. The company reports more than $1B in customer contracts across frontier AI labs and clouds. A backlog that size has to be delivered on a chip nobody outside Jane Street has run, which is exactly when a brand needs to be known.
why_now.label: Three prices in eight months

why_now.text: Eight AI partnerships were signed in Formula 1 in the six months to May 2026: Anthropic at Williams, Oracle's strategy agent at Red Bull, CoreWeave at Aston Martin, TWG AI exclusive at Cadillac, and Groq, an inference-chip rival, at McLaren. The buyers Etched sells to, frontier labs and clouds, are the people in F1's suites.
why_now.label: The category has already bought F1

why_now.text: Teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. The United States GP in Austin in late October, Mexico City and Las Vegas in November sit inside the window; a deal agreed before Austin can be announced at any of them.
why_now.label: Calendar window

why_team.text: The AI lane is the most-sold technology category on the 2026 grid and it is taken almost everywhere: TWG AI is Cadillac's primary and exclusive AI partner; Groq is at McLaren; AMD, Snapdragon and Meta AI at Mercedes; Cognition, CoreWeave and ARM at Aston Martin; Oracle at Red Bull; Anthropic at Williams. Audi's technical roster runs to NinjaOne, Extreme Networks, JigSpace and ElevenLabs for voice AI, and stops there: no inference, compute or chip partner.
why_team.label: A debut works team with the lane open

why_team.text: Audi entered as a full works team in 2026 after taking over Sauber, with the chassis at Hinwil, the power unit at Neuburg and a technology centre at Bicester; Mattia Binotto leads after Jonathan Wheatley left two rounds into the season, with James Key on the chassis and Stefan Dreyer on the power unit. A first-season German engineering programme is assembling its technical identity now, and a chip company with one named customer needs exactly that stage.
why_team.label: A team buying technology stories

why_team.text: Both are open in this lane. Haas is the American privateer and the natural home for a commodity-versus-premium story (the desk's Positron case points there); Alpine has no US home race and a roster built around consumer brands. Audi is the works team whose whole 2026 narrative is engineering credibility, which is what Etched's silicon sells.
why_team.label: Why not Haas or Alpine

why_team.text: Austin in late October, Mexico City and Las Vegas in November: three North American rounds inside the window for a San Jose company whose customers are American labs and clouds.
why_team.label: Where it activates

ruled_out.reason: TWG AI is primary and exclusive AI partner; Core Scientific holds the data-centre lane.
Groq, a direct inference-chip rival, is a partner.
AMD, Snapdragon and Meta AI occupy the chip and AI lanes.
Cognition, CoreWeave and ARM occupy AI, GPU cloud and chip design.
Oracle is title partner and runs the team's AI strategy agent.
Anthropic is the multi-year AI partner.
IBM and HP crowd enterprise technology and AI.
Dynatrace and Confluent crowd the data-infrastructure lane.
Open but not chosen: the desk's Positron case points there and the underdog story fits that company better; still a live alternative.
Open but not chosen: no US home race, a consumer-led roster; the named fallback.

brief_data.bottom_line: $700M at $21B with the first rack in a customer's hands and $1B of contracts to deliver, an inference-chip rival already on a McLaren, and a debut works team with no inference partner. A chip that runs one model family and a company with no marketing chief hold it at 75.

brief_data.the_case_p1: The round brought in Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia, Andreessen Horowitz, Tiger Global, Bain Capital Ventures and Blackstone behind Jane Street, which took delivery of the first Sohu rack in July and is deploying it into its own workloads; the company reports more than $1B in customer contracts across frontier AI labs and clouds. It follows a $300M Series C at $10.3B in July led by Sequoia. A $500M Stripes-led raise at $5B closed in December 2025. Sohu is built on TSMC's 4-nanometre process; founders Gavin Uberti, Chris Zhu and Robert Wachen started the company in 2022.
brief_data.the_case_p2: Inference silicon has already bought a Formula 1 seat: Groq is on a McLaren, and eight AI partnerships were signed on the grid in the six months to May, with Anthropic at Williams, Oracle's strategy agent at Red Bull and TWG AI exclusive at Cadillac. Every one of those sells a model or a cloud; Etched sells the chip underneath, and it has a customer running it.

brief_data.why_team_para: Audi Revolut F1 Team is a debut works entry under Mattia Binotto, and its technical roster carries NinjaOne, Extreme Networks and ElevenLabs for voice AI, but no inference or compute partner: the lane is taken at Cadillac (TWG AI, exclusive), McLaren (Groq), Mercedes (AMD, Snapdragon, Meta AI), Aston Martin (Cognition, CoreWeave), Red Bull (Oracle) and Williams (Anthropic). A German engineering brand in its first season buys technology stories; a chip company with one customer needs one.
brief_data.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Inference Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, through Sohu's first production generation and its successor. Estimated $5-8M a year, part-payable in Sohu racks the team would otherwise lease as cloud inference. Scope: sidepod placement, naming of the team's inference cluster, Austin, Mexico City and Las Vegas hospitality, and a content series on the cost of a token.
brief_data.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  Two price marks in a month, a first rack in a customer's hands and a $1B backlog to deliver: the company has to be known before the racks are. Teams close 2027 rosters in the fourth quarter; Austin in late October, Mexico City and Las Vegas sit inside the window.
brief_data.decision_maker_bio: Uberti co-founded Etched in 2022 with Chris Zhu and Robert Wachen, Thiel Fellows who left Harvard to build it, and runs a company with no marketing or commercial officer listed. Path: Robert Wachen, co-founder and Chief Operating Officer; Mark Rose, Chief Technology Officer.
brief_data.decision_maker_role: Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer, Etched
brief_data.opening_angle_intro: Lead with the customer, not the valuation.
brief_data.opening_angle_quote: “Gavin, Jane Street is running your rack and Groq is on a McLaren. Audi is a works team in its first season with no inference partner, and the 2027 roster closes this quarter. 25 minutes before Austin?”
